king gizzard & the lizard wizard|fishing.fact: King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's title track "Fishing for Fishies" is a warped nursery rhyme against recreational fishing - when asked what inspired the 2019 album's title, Stu Mackenzie simply wrote, "hunting makes me sad." Its music video, directed by Jason Galea, has the band floating on a raft past an alligator playing electric piano.

rilo kiley|science vs. romance.fact: Rilo Kiley's "Science Vs. Romance," from 2001's Take Offs and Landings, was written by Jenny Lewis and Blake Sennett - Stereogum later ranked it among the band's ten best songs.

mitski|i'll change for you.fact: Mitski's "I'll Change for You," the second single from 2026's Nothing's About to Happen to Me, came from wanting to write "a song about being pathetic" - channeling the irrational urge to beg an ex to take you back, in Mitski's own words.

sufjan stevens|with my whole heart.fact: Sufjan Stevens released "With My Whole Heart" alongside "Love Yourself" as a Pride Month single in 2019, with proceeds from companion T-shirts going to organizations supporting LGBTQ youth.

pavement|spit on a stranger.fact: Pavement's "Spit on a Stranger" opens 1999's Terror Twilight, the band's Nigel Godrich-produced final album - its single also included the deep cut "Harness Your Hopes," which years later, thanks to Spotify's algorithm, unexpectedly became the band's most-streamed song.

real estate|crime.fact: Real Estate's "Crime" comes from their self-titled 2009 debut, which Pitchfork gave an 8.5 and its Best New Music tag - an early sign of the acclaim the Ridgewood, New Jersey band would keep earning.

band of horses|the great salt lake.fact: Band of Horses' "The Great Salt Lake," from 2006's Everything All the Time, isn't really about the Great Salt Lake at all - frontman Ben Bridwell has said the imagery mostly pulls from Lake Murray, a reservoir in his home state of South Carolina, mixed with stories about friends from Salt Lake City.

sweeping promises|accent.fact: Sweeping Promises' "Accent," from 2026's You Say I Romanticize, is built around what the band calls a "cicadence" - a flapping, insectoid post-punk rhythm - wrestling with the uneasy feeling of trying to express yourself in a world that can make you feel like you're speaking a foreign language.

spiritualized|ladies & gentlemen we are.fact: Spiritualized's title track "Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space" borrows its melody from both Pachelbel's Canon in D and Elvis Presley's "Can't Help Falling in Love" - the album opens with band member Kate Radley's flat, deadpan voice on a phone recording saying the title phrase. NME ranked the 1997 album its #1 record of the year, ahead of Radiohead's OK Computer.

sparks|the number one song in heaven.fact: Sparks' "The Number One Song in Heaven" was written and produced with Giorgio Moroder after the Mael brothers heard his production on Donna Summer's "I Feel Love" and decided to ditch their guitars for synthesizers - it became a UK top-20 hit and, in 1997, was re-recorded with vocals from Bronski Beat's Jimmy Somerville.

beirut|gallipoli.fact: Beirut's title track "Gallipoli" came from a chance encounter - Zach Condon stumbled into a brass band procession carrying a saint's statue through the Italian town of Gallipoli, with church bells ringing and the band's sound bouncing off the narrow streets. He wrote the entire song the next day in one sitting, pausing only to eat.

cake|comfort eagle.fact: CAKE's title track "Comfort Eagle" is more widely known by its repeated hook, "Building a Religion" - frontman John McCrea wrote it as a metaphor for the marketing and propaganda that disguises what a product actually is. Fans voted it in as the album's second single, but its release was canceled after the September 11 attacks.

father john misty|pure comedy.fact: Father John Misty's title track "Pure Comedy" first previewed live at a December 2016 benefit concert for Seattle Children's Hospital - its opening verse is an almost direct paraphrase of an unplanned rant he delivered on stage at a festival earlier that year.

pickwick|turncoat.fact: Pickwick's "Turncoat" was the lead single from 2017's LoveJoys - the band's first album with producer Erik Blood, whose experimental tinkering pushed their sound toward a more psychedelic, kinetic direction.

toro y moi|so many details.fact: Toro y Moi's "So Many Details," the lead single from 2013's Anything in Return, was written, produced, and performed entirely by Chaz Bundick himself - Pitchfork called it a leap forward in his songwriting after his move from South Carolina to Berkeley, California.

wild nothing|only heather.fact: Wild Nothing's "Only Heather" comes from 2012's Nocturne - Jack Tatum's second album under the Wild Nothing name, which he began recording alone in Blacksburg, Virginia back in 2009.

twisted teens|when we first met.fact: Twisted Teens' "When We First Met" comes from The Holy Cross Tigers on Sub Pop - the New Orleans garage-punk duo of Caspian Hollywell and Ramon "RJ" Santos blend the street-level grit of The Gun Club with early-punk urgency and dusty country-blues storytelling.

king tuff|landline.fact: King Tuff's "Landline," from 2026's MOO, was recorded entirely on his Tascam 338 tape machine - the same one he used on his very first album, Was Dead, years earlier.

belle and sebastian|i don't know what yo.fact: Belle and Sebastian's "I Don't Know What You See In Me" marked a first for the band - their first-ever co-write with an outside songwriter, Scottish producer Wuh Oh (Peter Ferguson), on the lead single from 2023's Late Developers.

squid|paddling.fact: Squid's "Paddling," from 2021's Bright Green Field, was a longtime live staple years before its release - the band started writing it back when they were still teenagers living in Brighton, and it explores the tension between simple pleasures and modern consumerism through the lens of The Wind in the Willows.

diiv|kid.fact: DIIV's "Kid" comes from 2012's Oshin, the band's shoegaze-leaning debut - frontman Zachary Cole Smith has said Malian guitarist Baba Salah's record Borey shaped how he approached melody on the album.

ramones|gimme gimme shock treatment.fact: Ramones' "Gimme Gimme Shock Treatment," from 1977's Leave Home, was written by Dee Dee and Johnny Ramone at artist Arturo Vega's loft - the title nods to electroconvulsive therapy, filtered through the band's usual dark, satirical humor rather than anything to be taken literally.

beck|run away.fact: Beck's "Run Away," from 2026's Ride Lonesome, was mixed by longtime collaborator Nigel Godrich - its Tokyo-set music video stars Golden Globe-winning actor Tadanobu Asano, known for roles in Shogun and Thor: Ragnarok.

courtney barnett|need a little time.fact: Courtney Barnett's "Need a Little Time," the second single from 2018's Tell Me How You Really Feel, is about needing space in a relationship - its music video, directed by Danny Cohen, follows Barnett as a cosmic traveler morphing through time and space.

r.e.m.|daysleeper.fact: R.E.M.'s "Daysleeper" was the first single from 1998's Up - Michael Stipe wrote the lyrics after noticing the word "Daysleeper" on an apartment door and wondering about the life of the person living behind it. The music itself had actually been written years earlier, during the New Adventures in Hi-Fi sessions, but sat unused until Stipe found words for it.

wishy|sensational.fact: Wishy's "Sensational" grew out of a bassline Mitch Collins kept noodling on during soundchecks - it's a stylistic left turn from their earlier singles on 2026's Nature's Pill, its music video built from an animated collage of 3,000 cut-outs of the band.

the modern lovers|astral plane.fact: The Modern Lovers' "Astral Plane" was produced by John Cale of the Velvet Underground during their mid-1970s demo sessions - Jonathan Richman's lyrics turn a rejected pickup line into a promise to meet someone on a higher plane of existence instead.

stephen malkmus and the jicks|real emoti.fact: Stephen Malkmus and the Jicks' title track "Real Emotional Trash" stretches past ten minutes, built around an extended midsection of interlocking guitar solos - the album was recorded at SnowGhost Music in Whitefish, Montana, and Foxtrot Studio in Chicago.

kevin morby|i have been to the mountain.fact: Kevin Morby's "I Have Been to the Mountain," from 2016's Singing Saw, is one of his most richly orchestrated songs - built around mariachi horns, an angelic choir, and psychedelic guitar, recorded with Sam Cohen in Woodstock, New York after Morby started writing on an old piano that came with a new house.

elastica|stutter.fact: Elastica's debut single "Stutter" sold out its limited 1,500-copy pressing in a single day and shot to #1 on the UK indie charts - on the strength of just that one single and a couple of gigs, the band was voted Best New Band in Melody Maker's year-end readers' poll.

bat for lashes|the hunger.fact: Bat for Lashes' "The Hunger," from 2019's Lost Girls, started with an old '80s synth organ sound Natasha Khan was playing around with before co-writer/producer Charles Scott IV added bass - the whole album grew out of a screenplay Khan had been writing, inspired by '80s vampire and coming-of-age films.

soccer mommy|rings of saturn.fact: Soccer Mommy's "Rings of Saturn" was Sophie Allison's first new song in two years, produced by Elliott Kozel - she's said she wrote it during a hard stretch when she'd take a telescope out into the yard to look at the moon and planets, finding that feeling small could take some of the weight off.

jungle|i've been in love (feat. channel.fact: Jungle's "I've Been In Love," featuring Channel Tres, comes from 2023's Volcano - bandmember Josh Lloyd-Watson has called it "the most honest record" Jungle has made, an extension of the group's long-running love for soul music.

chvrches|roses.fact: Chvrches' "Roses" marked the band's first new music in three years - the chorus interpolates the old English nursery rhyme "Ring a Ring o' Roses," folded into a heavier, more guitar-driven sound than the band has leaned into before.

thom yorke|harrowdown hill.fact: Thom Yorke's "Harrowdown Hill" was the first single from his 2006 solo debut The Eraser, reaching #23 on the UK singles chart - the song actually dates back to the sessions for Radiohead's Hail to the Thief, though Yorke felt it never quite worked as a Radiohead song.

buck meek|can i mend it?.fact: Buck Meek's "Can I Mend It?," from 2026's The Mirror, was produced by his Big Thief bandmate James Krivchenia - the album also features Adrianne Lenker on vocals, plus contributions from harpist Mary Lattimore and composer Alex Somers on synths.

grizzly bear|losing all sense.fact: Grizzly Bear's "Losing All Sense," from 2017's Painted Ruins, started as the oldest demo in the band's pile - Chris Taylor sped up its original guitar riff and added a bass line, then Daniel Rossen layered in melody, passing it back and forth for years before it took final shape. Its music video features actress Busy Philipps.

the smiths|this night has opened my eyes.fact: The Smiths' "This Night Has Opened My Eyes" was inspired by the play A Taste of Honey - Morrissey has said the play accounts for at least half of his reason for writing in the first place. The version released on 1984's Hatful of Hollow actually comes from a BBC Radio 1 John Peel session, not a proper studio single.

cheekface|life in a bag.fact: Cheekface's "Life in a Bag," from 2024's It's Sorted, was written by all three band members - Amanda Tannen, Greg Katz, and Mark Edwards - and produced by longtime collaborator Greg Cortez.

arlo parks|pegasus (feat. phoebe bridger.fact: Arlo Parks' "Pegasus," featuring Phoebe Bridgers, comes from 2023's My Soft Machine - it was produced by Paul Epworth (Adele, Florence and the Machine) alongside Brockhampton's Romil Hemnani and producer Baird.

gang of four|paralysed.fact: Gang of Four's "Paralysed" opens 1981's Solid Gold, recorded at Abbey Road Studios in London - written by Andy Gill and Jon King, it's built around the memorable line "Paradise, if you can earn it."

tame impala|borderline.fact: Tame Impala's "Borderline" debuted live on Saturday Night Live in March 2019 before Kevin Parker had even finished writing the lyrics, ad-libbing much of it on the spot - listen closely after he sings "like a train" and you can hear an actual passing train in the mix.

wild pink|dead for a sec.fact: Wild Pink's "Dead for a Sec," from 2026's Still Coming Down, features MJ Lenderman harmonizing on the chorus and tearing into a Crazy Horse-style guitar solo over the outro - the album was recorded in just one week at Drop of Sun studios in Asheville with producer Alex Farrar.

unknown mortal orchestra|ur life one nig.fact: Unknown Mortal Orchestra's "Ur Life One Night," from 2015's Multi-Love, has a music video shot in India, inspired by traditional Asian art and Indian magical-realism - Ruban Nielson has said he specifically wanted to work with a director there, surprised he'd never made a video in the country with the world's biggest film industry.

ramones|beat on the brat.fact: Ramones' "Beat on the Brat" grew out of Joey Ramone watching a spoiled kid's meltdown in his Forest Hills, Queens apartment lobby - the band played it live for over a year before recording it, and its opening chord change was lifted straight from bubblegum-pop songs like "Yummy Yummy Yummy." U2 later covered it for a 2003 Ramones tribute album.

r.e.m.|man on the moon.fact: R.E.M.'s "Man on the Moon" started life as an instrumental called "C to D Slide" that almost got scrapped - Michael Stipe couldn't find lyrics for it until Andy Kaufman's oddball legacy, including his pro-wrestling stunts and Elvis impersonation, gave him something to write about. The song later lent its title to the 1999 Jim Carrey biopic about Kaufman.

wishy|mona lisa.fact: Wishy's "Mona Lisa," from 2026's Nature's Pill, is a slacker-pop love song that closes out with a minute and a half of sing-along "oohs" and "aahs" - frontman Kevin Krauter met his bandmates in high school back in Indianapolis.

chvrches|leave a trace.fact: Chvrches' "Leave a Trace" was the first single from 2015's Every Open Eye, self-produced by the band - Lauren Mayberry has called it a "middle finger mic-drop" of a song, about reaching the point in an argument where you realize nothing more is going to change. Rolling Stone later named it one of the best songs of 2015.

caribou|volume.fact: Volume, from Caribou's 2024 album Honey, samples the 1987 dance hit Pump Up the Volume by MARRS. Dan Snaith, who records as Caribou, released it as a single on July 31, 2024, ahead of the album's October 4 release.

dry cleaning|joy.fact: Joy closes Dry Cleaning's third album, Secret Love (4AD, January 2026), which was produced by Welsh musician Cate Le Bon. The band made demos at Wilco's studio, The Loft, in Chicago, then re-recorded the album at Black Box Studios in France's Loire Valley.

cassandra jenkins|only one.fact: Only One was the lead single from Cassandra Jenkins' 2024 album My Light, My Destroyer. She wrote it with Stephanie Marziano, and it was inspired by a Groundhog Day feeling of repeating the same situation over and over.

radiohead|lotus flower.fact: The video for Lotus Flower, from The King of Limbs, was directed by Garth Jennings and choreographed by Wayne McGregor. Thom Yorke's dancing in it turned into the "Dancing Thom Yorke" internet meme in 2011.

wilco|the joke explained.fact: The Joke Explained is on Wilco's 2015 album Star Wars, which the band surprised fans with by releasing without advance announcement. The song is a fuzzy garage-rock number built around the line "I cry at a joke explained."

r.e.m.|driver 8.fact: Driver 8 is about the Southern Crescent, a passenger train that ran on Southern Railway lines until 1979. It is from R.E.M.'s 1985 album Fables of the Reconstruction, which was recorded at Livingston Studios in London with producer Joe Boyd.

r.e.m.|fall on me.fact: Fall on Me, from Lifes Rich Pageant (1986), started as a song about acid rain and became one of R.E.M.'s early environmental songs. It was the album's first single and reached number 94 on the Billboard Hot 100.

massive attack|teardrop.fact: Teardrop features vocals by Elizabeth Fraser of the Cocteau Twins, who also wrote the lyrics. The band had reportedly planned a Madonna vocal, but took a vote and went with Fraser. It later became the opening theme of the TV series House.

devo|(i can't get no) satisfaction.fact: DEVO's herky-jerky remake of the Rolling Stones' Satisfaction was their 1977 second single. Because their label worried about permission, Gerald Casale and Mark Mothersbaugh flew to New York to play it for Mick Jagger, who approved. Brian Eno produced their 1978 debut album.

hotline tnt|break right.fact: Break Right, from Hotline TNT's album Raspberry Moon, was the first song the band wrote as a full group. The instrumental parts came from guitarist Lucky Hunter, bassist Haylen Trammel and drummer Mike Ralston rather than frontman Will Anderson.

frankie cosmos|apathy.fact: Apathy is on Frankie Cosmos's 2018 album Vessel. Greta Kline began as a solo bedroom-recording artist, and Vessel showed the project growing into a full-band DIY indie-pop sound.

panda bear & sonic boom|a ? of when.fact: A ? of WHEN is the second album from Panda Bear and Sonic Boom, following their 2022 debut Reset. It is built from loops of harp and steel drum, plus harpist Mary Lattimore, pedal steel from Zena Kay, and even samples of a Mexico City mariachi band.

black country, new road|the big spin.fact: The Big Spin appears on Live at Bush Hall, recorded over two nights in December 2022 at Bush Hall in London. The band debuted a whole set of brand-new songs live there before any of them had studio versions.

tunde adebimpe|god knows.fact: God Knows is from Thee Black Boltz, the debut solo album by TV on the Radio frontman Tunde Adebimpe (Sub Pop, 2025). Adebimpe produced it with Wilder Zoby.

sufjan stevens|the ascension.fact: The Ascension is the title track of Sufjan Stevens' 2020 album, a 15-song, roughly 80-minute record on Asthmatic Kitty. It marked a big shift to electronic sounds after the quiet acoustic Carrie & Lowell.

mac demarco|chamber of reflection.fact: Chamber of Reflection is the one Salad Days song where synths replace Mac DeMarco's usual chorused guitar; the lead synth is a Roland JX-3P. The title comes from a Freemasonry meditation room, which DeMarco compared to his home studio.

the national|demons.fact: Demons was the first single from The National's 2013 album Trouble Will Find Me. The album was recorded across several studios, from upstate New York to Los Angeles and the Michelberger Hotel in Berlin.

wednesday|chosen to deserve.fact: Chosen to Deserve was the January 2023 single that announced Wednesday's fifth album, Rat Saw God (Dead Oceans, April 2023). Songwriter Karly Hartzman has said hearing the Drive-By Truckers song Let There Be Rock helped inspire it.

iron & wine|last of your rock 'n' roll h.fact: Last of Your Rock 'n' Roll Heroes is from Iron & Wine's 2018 Sub Pop EP Weed Garden, a set of six songs left over from the sessions for Sam Beam's album Beast Epic.

beirut|fisher island sound.fact: Fisher Island Sound was released in October 2021 to announce Beirut's album Artifacts. Zach Condon wrote it while staying at bandmate Ben Lanz's old family cottage on the Connecticut coast, which sits on the body of water named in the title.

real estate|had to hear.fact: Had to Hear opens Real Estate's third album, Atlas (March 2014), and was released as a single that August. It shows off the band's signature chiming guitar chords and Martin Courtney's gentle vocals, and critics compared the album's opening pair to Galaxie 500.

the avalanches feat. mgmt & johnny marr|.fact: The Divine Chord is from The Avalanches' third album, We Will Always Love You (December 2020). It pairs MGMT's Andrew VanWyngarden on vocals with guitar from Johnny Marr, formerly of The Smiths.

toro y moi|freelance.fact: Freelance was the lead single from Toro y Moi's 2019 album Outer Peace. Chaz Bear wrote it about his return to the San Francisco Bay Area after living in Portland, Oregon.

wild nothing|nocturne.fact: Nocturne is the title track of Wild Nothing's 2012 second album on Captured Tracks. Jack Tatum recorded it in a real studio in Brooklyn with producer Nicolas Vernhes, after making the debut, Gemini, entirely on a laptop.

flock of dimes|two.fact: Two, the first single from Flock of Dimes' 2021 album Head of Roses (Sub Pop), came from Wye Oak's Jenn Wasner going solo. Nick Sanborn of Sylvan Esso produced the album.

waxahatchee|never been wrong.fact: Never Been Wrong was the second single from Waxahatchee's fourth album, Out in the Storm (2017). Katie Crutchfield sings it over big, blown-out guitars.

xtc|the mayor of simpleton.fact: Mayor of Simpleton was the first single from XTC's 1989 album Oranges & Lemons and hit number 1 on Billboard's Alternative Songs chart. Andy Partridge started it as a reggae song before scrapping that and rewriting it around a chiming, droning guitar figure.

m83|oceans niagara.fact: Oceans Niagara is a single from M83's 2023 album Fantasy, the project of French musician Anthony Gonzalez. It also has an accompanying short film.

low|words.fact: Words opens Low's 1994 debut album, I Could Live in Hope. The band formed in Duluth, Minnesota around Alan Sparhawk and Mimi Parker, and critics filed their hushed, spare sound under the label slowcore.

pixies|caribou.fact: Caribou is on Come On Pilgrim, the Pixies' 1987 debut mini-album. The band's next record, Surfer Rosa, was recorded that winter with producer Steve Albini.

arlo parks ft. sampha|senses.fact: Senses pairs Arlo Parks with Mercury Prize winner Sampha and is from her 2026 album Ambiguous Desire, her follow-up to 2023's My Soft Machine.

weyes blood|andromeda.fact: Andromeda was the lead single from Weyes Blood's Titanic Rising (2019), co-produced by Natalie Mering and Jonathan Rado. Its space-themed video was partly filmed in 2018 but not finished until 2024, with Mering playing both an astronaut and an alien riding a meteor.

the decemberists|sons & daughters.fact: Sons & Daughters closes The Decemberists' 2006 album The Crane Wife, which was loosely inspired by a Japanese folktale about a bird who takes human form. Colin Meloy's bouzouki gives the singable, round-style finale its warmth.

u.s. girls|like james said.fact: Like James Said is from U.S. Girls' 2025 album Scratch It (4AD). Meg Remy wrote it with longtime collaborator Rich Morel, borrowing James Brown's advice to "dance until you feel better."

gorillaz|the happy dictator.fact: The Happy Dictator, featuring the art-pop duo Sparks, was the lead single from Gorillaz's 2025 album The Mountain. The collaboration was teased when Sparks posted a photo with Damon Albarn at his Studio 13, and Russell Mael joined Albarn for a performance on Jimmy Kimmel Live.

boygenius|$20.fact: $20 was one of three singles boygenius released together in January 2023 to announce their debut album, The Record (Interscope, March 2023). Julien Baker wrote it and sings lead, with Phoebe Bridgers and Lucy Dacus adding harmonies. The album gave all three members their first number-one albums in the UK.

tune-yards|heartbreak.fact: Heartbreak opens Tune-Yards' 2025 album Better Dreaming, their first since 2021's sketchy. Merrill Garbus and Nate Brenner build it from huge stacked vocal harmonies over a slow-jam beat full of clicks, pops and samples.

beach house|new romance.fact: New Romance is from Beach House's eighth album, the double album Once Twice Melody (Sub Pop, February 2022). It was released in four "chapters" starting in November 2021, and the song runs on a swirling, calliope-like synth loop.

kevin morby|die young.fact: Die Young is from Kevin Morby's 2026 album Little Wide Open (Dead Oceans). It grew out of a melody he wrote at a soundcheck in a small village in France in summer 2024 and finished in 2025.

friko|seven degrees.fact: Seven Degrees previewed Friko's second album, Something Worth Waiting For. The Evanston, Illinois band's Niko Kapetan says he'd misremembered the famous saying as "seven degrees of separation" instead of six, and the song is about staying close to people.

chastity|summer all over again.fact: Summer All Over Again comes from the self-titled 2024 album by Chastity, the project of Brandon Williams, released on Deathwish Inc. Williams described the mood as "that quiet melancholy, like when you're outside on a perfect day, and you miss your cue to be happy."

men i trust|carried away.fact: Carried Away is from the Montreal band Men I Trust's album Equus Caballus. The trio formed in 2014 around Emmanuelle Proulx, Jessy Caron and Dragos Chiriac, and this song even nods to hair-metal influences.

hovvdy|try try try.fact: Try Try Try is the lead single from Hovvdy's sixth album, Big World (August 2026). It was produced by longtime collaborator Ben Littlejohn and recorded in Nashville and Asheville, with Will Taylor and Charlie Martin arriving with only instrumentals rather than finished demos.

death cab for cutie|punching the flowers.fact: Punching the Flowers is from Death Cab for Cutie's eleventh album, I Built You a Tower (June 2026). It followed the singles Riptides and preceded Stone Over Water, and the album has a heavier rock feel than their recent records.

the smiths|frankly, mr. shankly.fact: Johnny Marr wrote the music for Frankly, Mr. Shankly in late summer 1985, around the same time as There Is a Light That Never Goes Out. It is a comic letter to a boss on The Queen Is Dead, and is widely reputed to be aimed at Rough Trade Records head Geoff Travis.

king gizzard & the lizard wizard|mars fo.fact: Mars for the Rich is from Infest the Rats' Nest (2019), King Gizzard's first full-on metal project, released between their microtonal and jam-heavy albums to show off how many styles the Australian band works in.

bright eyes|we are nowhere and it's now.fact: We Are Nowhere and It's Now is the second track on Bright Eyes' 2005 album I'm Wide Awake, It's Morning. Conor Oberst wanted a female voice up front on the song, and Emmylou Harris sings on it.

chicano batman|fly.fact: Fly was the first single from Chicano Batman's 2024 album Notebook Fantasy (ATO Records). The Los Angeles psych-soul band's follow-up single, Era Primavera, was inspired by singer Bardo's love of 1960s Latin ballads.

chicano batman|era primavera.fact: Era Primavera was the second single from Chicano Batman's 2024 album Notebook Fantasy. It's a symphonic love song inspired by vocalist and lyricist Bardo's fascination with 1960s Latin ballads.

dinosaur jr.|in a jar.fact: In a Jar is from Dinosaur Jr.'s 1987 album You're Living All Over Me. Lou Barlow's distorted, chunky bass is a huge part of the song, and J Mascis played it when the band later revisited their 1988 album Bug live.

mandy, indiana|cursive.fact: Cursive is from Mandy, Indiana's second album, Urgh (Sacred Bones, February 2026). The English-French noise band's 2023 debut, i've seen a way, was recorded in unusual spaces including caves, crypts and shopping malls.

daughter|not enough.fact: Not Enough was written during the sessions for Daughter's 2016 album Not to Disappear but left off it. The trio revisited it for the album's tenth anniversary and recorded it at London's Total Refreshment studio in November 2025.

black belt eagle scout|my blood runs thr.fact: My Blood Runs Through This Land is from The Land, The Water, The Sky (Saddle Creek, 2023). Katherine Paul, a member of the Swinomish Indian Tribal Community, made the album about her move from Portland back to her homelands, and Evan Benally Atwood directed the video.

angine de poitrine|sherpa.fact: Sherpa comes from the first EP by Angine de Poitrine, an anonymous duo from Saguenay, Quebec who play microtonal rock in polka-dot costumes and giant papier-mache masks. Their KEXP performance went viral, and guitarist Khn plays a double-necked microtonal guitar.

saint etienne|glad.fact: Glad was co-written and co-produced by Tom Rowlands of The Chemical Brothers, with Jez Williams of Doves on guitar. It came from International (September 2025), which Saint Etienne have said is their final studio album.

modest mouse|look how far....fact: Look How Far... was the first single from Modest Mouse's eighth studio album, An Eraser and a Maze (June 2026). Isaac Brock shares production credit with Jacknife Lee, Justin Raisen, Jeremy Sherrer and Suzy Shinn.

modest mouse|picking dragons' pockets.fact: Picking Dragons' Pockets, a single from Modest Mouse's 2026 album An Eraser and a Maze, opens with an intense drums-and-guitar intro over a synth undercurrent. The album was produced by Isaac Brock with Jacknife Lee, Justin Raisen, Jeremy Sherrer and Suzy Shinn.

youth lagoon|lucy takes a picture.fact: Lucy Takes a Picture is from Youth Lagoon's 2025 album Rarely Do I Dream (Fat Possum). Trevor Powers built the album around childhood home videos he found in his parents' basement, and he samples the tapes throughout.

cate le bon|always the same (ft. st. vin.fact: Always the Same was written during the sessions for Cate Le Bon's 2025 album Michelangelo Dying and released in January 2026 as a cousin to it. It reunited her with St. Vincent, whom she'd worked with on St. Vincent's 2024 album All Born Screaming.

bon iver|heavenly father.fact: Justin Vernon wrote Heavenly Father for the soundtrack of Zach Braff's film Wish I Was Here. After watching a rough cut, he started humming and the song's title phrase came out. It returned to streaming in 2026 as part of Bon Iver's VOLUMES archive series.

brittany howard|prove it to you.fact: Prove It to You, from Brittany Howard's 2024 album What Now, is a 1990s house-inspired dance track. Howard said she wanted to write a fun four-on-the-floor song, and critics have compared its feel to Underworld.

broadcast|follow the light.fact: Follow the Light was the first single from Spell Blanket (2024), a collection of demos that Broadcast singer Trish Keenan recorded between 2006 and 2009. It keeps the band's habit of building songs from short, repeating lyrics.

nation of language|tougher than the rest.fact: Nation of Language's version of Bruce Springsteen's Tougher Than the Rest came out in 2026 as a limited 7-inch on Sub Pop, pressed in just 1,000 copies. Singer Ian Richard Devaney says they used a Yamaha CS-80, the same synth model featured on Springsteen's 1987 Tunnel of Love sessions.

white lies|nothing on me.fact: Nothing On Me opens White Lies' seventh album, Night Light (Play It Again Sam, November 2025). The trio recorded the whole record in singer Harry McVeigh's spare room.

cindy lee|diamond jubilee.fact: Diamond Jubilee is the title track of a 32-song, two-hour album by Cindy Lee, the project of Patrick Flegel, formerly of the band Women. He self-released it in 2024 on his own label, and it was shortlisted for the Polaris Music Prize.

softcult|not sorry.fact: Not Sorry is from When a Flower Doesn't Grow, the debut full-length album (January 2026) from Softcult, the Ontario band made up of twins Mercedes and Phoenix Arn-Horn. The video came out the same day as the album.

snocaps|brand new city.fact: Snocaps is a band led by siblings Katie Crutchfield (Waxahatchee) and Allison Crutchfield, joined by MJ Lenderman and producer Brad Cook. Brand New City is from their self-titled 2025 album on Anti- Records.

stereolab|vermona f transistor.fact: Vermona F Transistor is from Instant Holograms on Metal Film (2025), Stereolab's first studio album in almost 15 years. The track features backing vocals from Molly Hansen Read, niece of former Stereolab guitarist Mary Hansen, and its title nods to Vermona, a maker of analog synthesizers.

sprints|heavy.fact: Heavy is from Letter to Self (January 2024), the debut album by SPRINTS, a garage-punk band formed in Dublin in 2019. Critics described the record as sounding like PJ Harvey fronting the Pixies.

jungle|all of the time.fact: All of the Time was released in August 2021 as a single from Jungle's third album, Loving in Stereo. The British group started in 2013 when London producers Josh Lloyd-Watson and Tom McFarland teamed up, and they release their music on their own label, Caiola Records.

foxwarren|sleeping.fact: Sleeping is from 2, the 2025 second album by Foxwarren, the band built around Canadian songwriter Andy Shauf with Dallas Bryson and brothers Darryl and Avery Kissick. Their self-titled debut came out in 2018.

tops|chlorine.fact: Chlorine is from Bury the Key (Ghostly International, August 2025), the first full-length from Montreal band TOPS since 2020's I Feel Alive. The band self-produced it and leaned into a darker, "sinister disco" edge while keeping their dreamy sophisti-pop sound.

khruangbin|connaissais de face.fact: Connaissais de Face first appeared on Khruangbin's album Mordechai. The Texas trio later reworked it as Connaissais de Face (Tiger?), a collaboration with Ginger Root, on their 2024 album A La Sala.

gwenno|utopia.fact: Gwenno's 2025 album Utopia is mostly in English, a change from her earlier records: 2018's Le Kov was written entirely in Cornish, one of the few albums in the language, and helped spark new interest in it.

ratboys|penny in the lake.fact: Penny in the Lake is from Singin' to an Empty Chair, the 2026 album from the Chicago band Ratboys. The song was released with a video and an announcement of a Chicago benefit show.

sault|smile and go.fact: Smile and Go is the fifth track on 7, the second album by British group SAULT, released in September 2019. Producer Inflo worked with vocalist Cleo Sol on it.

the weather station|window.fact: Window is the second single from The Weather Station's 2025 album Humanhood (Fat Possum). Tamara Lindeman co-produced the 13-track album with Marcus Paquin and recorded it in fall 2023 at Canterbury Music Company, mixing 1960s psychedelic pop, jazz and spoken-word collage.

wet leg|catch these fists.fact: Catch These Fists was the first single from Wet Leg's second album, moisturizer (July 2025), which Rhian Teasdale and Hester Chambers made with producer Dan Carey. They focused on making songs that would be fun to play live, and the album debuted at number one in the UK.

phoebe bridgers|liberty tree.fact: Liberty Tree, the tenth track on Phoebe Bridgers' third album, Lost Weekend (August 2026), is named for the Liberty Tree Mall in Danvers, Massachusetts. Bridgers turned the mall into the setting of a song about finding love in an unlikely place.

caribou|climbing.fact: Climbing, from Caribou's 2024 album Honey (Merge and City Slang), samples Just Friends by the duo Rene & Angela from 1981. The track leans into playful disco-funk with glittering synth arpeggios.

eaves wilder|everybody talks.fact: Everybody Talks, released in November 2025, was a single from Eaves Wilder's debut album, Little Miss Sunshine (Secretly Canadian, April 2026).

avalon emerson & priori|you're my world.fact: You're My World features Montreal artist Priori and was released in July 2025 ahead of Avalon Emerson's electronic indie-pop album Written Into Changes, credited to Avalon Emerson & the Charm.

avalon emerson|written into changes.fact: Written Into Changes is the title track of the second album of electronic indie-pop songs credited to Avalon Emerson & the Charm (2026). Emerson first became known as a DJ and dance-music producer before moving toward songwriting.

lala lala|even mountains erode.fact: Even Mountains Erode is track 2 on Lala Lala's 2026 album Heaven 2 (Sub Pop). Lillie West played almost everything on the record herself, working with co-producer Melina Duterte, who records as Jay Som.

tune-yards|how big is the rainbow.fact: How Big Is the Rainbow, a single from Tune-Yards' 2025 album Better Dreaming, is a clattering disco-house track. Its music video, directed by Dominic Mercurio, stars comedian and actress Star Amerasu.

parts & labor|endless cycle pt. 3 - bett.fact: Endless Cycle Pt. 3 is one part of a four-part, roughly 20-minute single that Brooklyn noise band Parts & Labor released to announce their comeback. It's on Set of All Sets (2026), a 79-minute double album and their first in about 15 years, made with a double-drummer lineup.

punchbag|pile of clothes.fact: Pile of Clothes is from I Am Obsessed, a five-track release from PUNCHBAG in April 2026. The South London brother-sister duo mixes the raw energy of punk with the exuberance of pop.

the sophs|sweetiepie.fact: The Sophs are a six-piece from Los Angeles who signed to Rough Trade after cold-emailing demos to label heads Geoff Travis and Jeannette Lee before ever playing a show. SWEETIEPIE, from their debut album GOLDSTAR (2026), pairs a deadpan, Weezer-like vocal with country twang and a jaw harp.

alex g|afterlife.fact: Afterlife is a single from Alex G's 2025 album Headlights (RCA Records). It is driven by mandolin and airy, bagpipe-like keyboards, and has been compared to The Waterboys' Celtic-tinged anthems.

juliana hatfield|popsicle.fact: Popsicle was a single from Juliana Hatfield's 2025 album Lightning Might Strike. Its video was directed by Paige Applin, and Hatfield has said the frozen summer treat is a symbol for the dread in her head, wrapped in bright pop sweetness.

closure in moscow|better ways.fact: The song, released as a single in March 2023, is from Soft Hell (October 2023), the album that ended a nine-year gap for Closure in Moscow. The Melbourne progressive rock band formed in 2006, and their previous album was 2014's Pink Lemonade.

the bug club|watching the omnibus.fact: Watching the Omnibus, the lead single from The Bug Club's seventh album Every Single Muscle (2026), runs just 79 seconds. The Welsh band recorded the 18-track album with Tom Rees at Rat Trap Studios in Cardiff, and Mikey Young mastered it.

cloud nothings|i'd get along.fact: I'd Get Along is the third track on Cloud Nothings' album Final Summer. Dylan Baldi has said his interest in doom metal during the pandemic pushed the guitars to be big and bulky, with a bouncy drum part and a poppy vocal melody on top.

weird nightmare|headful of rain.fact: Weird Nightmare is the solo project of Alex Edkins, longtime frontman of the noise-rock trio METZ. Headful of Rain opens his 2026 album Hoopla, which he made with Spoon's Jim Eno at Machines with Magnets studio.

corridor|mourir demain.fact: Mourir Demain is from Mimi (Sub Pop, 2024), the Montreal band Corridor's first album in five years, which is named after singer Jonathan Robert's cat. Making the record remotely pushed them away from seeing themselves as just a guitar band, and this song adds ascending synths.

frankie cosmos|pressed flower.fact: Pressed Flower opens Frankie Cosmos's 2025 album Different Talking (Sub Pop). Its video, directed by Adam Kolodny, stars comedy legend Tracey Ullman alongside the band.

shame|cutthroat.fact: Cutthroat is the title track of shame's fourth album (Dead Oceans, September 2025), produced by John Congleton and recorded at Salvation Studios in Brighton. The band also talked about being inspired by Brazilian music while making it.

buck meek|gasoline.fact: Gasoline is from The Mirror (2026), the fourth solo album from Big Thief guitarist Buck Meek. Big Thief drummer James Krivchenia produced it, and Adrianne Lenker sings backup vocals on the song.

bat for lashes|daniel.fact: Daniel was the lead single from Bat for Lashes' second album, Two Suns (2009), and became her best-selling single, reaching number 36 in the UK. Her debut, Fur and Gold, had been nominated for the 2007 Mercury Prize.

lucy dacus|planting tomatoes.fact: Planting Tomatoes was Lucy Dacus's first new music of 2026, first released as a Record Store Day exclusive 7-inch in April before reaching streaming. She shot its lyric video herself in Tokyo.

friko|still around.fact: Still Around is from Friko's second album, Something Worth Waiting For (April 2026), which was produced by John Congleton. The album stretches into noise-rock, avant-garde classical touches and 1970s-style symphonic ballads.

arlo parks|blades.fact: Blades is a single from Arlo Parks' second album, My Soft Machine (2023). She wrote it with producer Paul Epworth, and it has a glitterball-disco feel.

feeble little horse|rewind.fact: Rewind, which runs only about two minutes, is one of 11 songs on bitknot, the third album from the Pittsburgh band feeble little horse. They announced it on May 21, 2026 and released it just five days later.

feeble little horse|dior.fact: Dior is from bitknot, the third album by Pittsburgh band feeble little horse. It came out May 26, 2026, just five days after it was announced, and follows their 2023 album Girl with Fish.

good dear good|slick.fact: Slick is from sook, a 2025 album by Good Dear Good, an indie pop-rock band from Halifax, Nova Scotia.

good dear good|better off dead.fact: Better Off Dead is from sook, a 2025 album by Good Dear Good, an indie pop-rock band from Halifax, Nova Scotia.

current joys|lullaby for the lost.fact: Lullaby for the Lost is a six-minute ballad and the third single from Current Joys' 12th album, East My Love (Secretly Canadian, 2024). Nick Rattigan wrote the country-tinged album alone in the woods in Tennessee, with no cell reception.

angine de poitrine|sarniezz.fact: Sarniezz is from Vol. II (April 2026), the second album by the masked Quebec duo Angine de Poitrine. Their live KEXP performance of the song went viral and racked up millions of views.

kim gordon|not today.fact: Not Today was the lead single from Play Me (Matador, March 2026), Kim Gordon's third solo album. Justin Raisen produced it, as he did her Grammy-nominated 2024 album The Collective, but this time the sound leans on krautrock-style repetition.

tunde adebimpe|drop.fact: Drop was the second single from Thee Black Boltz, the 2025 debut solo album from TV on the Radio's Tunde Adebimpe. It was produced by his bandmate Jahphet Landis and builds out from a looped beatboxing pattern.

mitski|my love mine all mine.fact: My Love Mine All Mine, with country-flavored piano and pedal steel, was the third single from Mitski's 2023 album The Land Is Inhospitable and So Are We. It became her commercial breakthrough: her first Billboard Hot 100 entry, peaking at number 26, and it reached number 8 in the UK.

slow fiction|turning down flowers.fact: turning down flowers is the six-minute closer of dollhouse, the debut album from New York band Slow Fiction (Tight Knit Records, 2026). The band produced it themselves, with Sonny DiPerri mixing.

amber arcades|come with me.fact: Come with Me opens Fading Lines (2016), the debut album by Dutch musician Annelotte de Graaf as Amber Arcades. She flew to New York to record it with producer Ben Greenberg, and members of Quilt and Real Estate served as her backing band.

diiv|everyone out.fact: Everyone Out is the sixth track on DIIV's 2024 album Frog in Boiling Water. It swaps their usual guitar wash for acoustic guitar, layered tape loops and synthesizers, in a sound some critics compared to early Smashing Pumpkins.

wishy|persuasion.fact: Persuasion is the fourth track on Triple Seven (2024), the debut album by Wishy of Indianapolis. Kevin Krauter teaches drum and guitar lessons, and Nina Pitchkites is a seamstress who makes embroidered merch for the band.

big thief|incomprehensible.fact: Incomprehensible opens Big Thief's sixth album, Double Infinity (4AD, 2025), their first as a trio. The band recorded it live over about three weeks at the Power Station studio in New York City, with producer Dom Monks.

wild pink|air drumming fix you.fact: Air Drumming Fix You, released in March 2024, was Wild Pink's first new music since 2022's ILYSM and came with the band signing to Fire Talk Records. The title nods to Coldplay's Fix You, and the song ends with saxophones.

iron & wine|in your ocean.fact: In Your Ocean was the lead single from Hen's Teeth (Sub Pop, February 2026), Iron & Wine's eighth album. Sam Beam has described it as a sibling record to Light Verse, his 2024 Grammy-nominated album.

beabadoobee|all i did was dream of you.fact: All I Did Was Dream of You, released in March 2026, features vocals from The Marias' Maria Zardoya. Its video was shot in and around Vilnius, Lithuania, and takes inspiration from Yorgos Lanthimos's film Bugonia.

king gizzard & the lizard wizard|gondii.fact: Gondii is on King Gizzard's 2022 album Ice, Death, Planets, Lungs, Mushrooms and Lava. The band recorded most of it in about a week, improvising with only a tempo, a key signature and a title to start each day. The name refers to the parasite Toxoplasma gondii.

devo|girl u want.fact: Girl U Want was the first single from DEVO's third album, Freedom of Choice (1980), which was produced by Bob Margouleff and also included Whip It. Mark Mothersbaugh and Gerald Casale, who founded the band in Akron, Ohio, wrote it.

the postal service|turn around.fact: Turn Around was left off The Postal Service's 2003 album Give Up and only surfaced on the Deluxe 10th Anniversary Edition in 2013. The band's name came from how they made the record: Jimmy Tamborello mailed CDs of electronic tracks from Los Angeles to Ben Gibbard in Seattle, who added vocals and melodies.

faye webster|but not kiss.fact: But Not Kiss is the second track on Faye Webster's 2024 album Underdressed at the Symphony, recorded at Sonic Ranch in Texas. The title comes from her habit of slipping into Atlanta Symphony Orchestra concerts, which she has said felt almost like therapy.

future islands|the ink well.fact: The Ink Well first came out in 2010 as one side of a split 7-inch single with Lonnie Walker on Friends Records, produced and mixed by Chester Endersby Gwazda. In 2026 Future Islands revived it for their rarities compilation From a Hole in the Floor to a Fountain of Youth.

the strokes|falling out of love.fact: Falling Out of Love is the second single from The Strokes' seventh album, Reality Awaits (2026), produced by Rick Rubin. Recording began in 2022 in Costa Rica and continued at Rubin's Shangri-La and The Mansion studios in California.

radiohead|ful stop.fact: Ful Stop, from Radiohead's 2016 album A Moon Shaped Pool, features extra drums from Clive Deamer, who had played with the band on The King of Limbs tour. The strings and choir on the album were arranged by guitarist Jonny Greenwood and performed by the London Contemporary Orchestra.

been stellar|adored.fact: Adored was the second single of 2025 from New York five-piece Been Stellar, following Breakaway, ahead of their debut album Scream From New York, NY. The band is Sam Slocum, Skyler Knapp, Laila Wayans, Nico Brunstein and Nando Dale.

english teacher|nearly daffodils.fact: Nearly Daffodils was produced by Marta Salgoni, who has worked with Bjork and Black Midi, and was named one of Time magazine's 10 best songs of 2023. The Leeds four-piece's debut album, This Could Be Texas, went on to win the 2024 Mercury Prize.

jeff tweedy|enough.fact: Enough is a single from Jeff Tweedy's 30-song triple album Twilight Override, released September 26, 2025. The album features his sons Spencer and Sammy Tweedy alongside Chicago collaborators including James Elkington, Sima Cunningham, Macie Stewart and Liam Kazar.

widowspeak|if you change.fact: If You Change is the lead single from Widowspeak's seventh album, Roses (2026, Captured Tracks), their first studio album since 2022's The Jacket. Molly Hamilton and Robert Earl Thomas recorded it at the Old Carpet Factory studio on the Greek island of Hydra.

mac demarco|holy.fact: Holy is from Mac DeMarco's 2025 album Guitar, which he recorded November 16-28, 2024 at his home studio in Los Angeles. He made the whole record himself, apart from mastering by David Ives, and filmed the Holy music video himself too.

purity ring|place of my own.fact: Place of My Own is from Purity Ring's 2025 self-titled fourth album, a concept record that works as the soundtrack to an imagined role-playing video game. The duo cited games like Nier Automata and Final Fantasy X as inspiration.

friko|choo choo.fact: Choo Choo was a single ahead of Friko's second album, Something Worth Waiting For (2026). The Chicago duo of Niko Kapetan and Bailey Minzenberger first broke out with their 2024 debut, Where we've been, Where we go from here.

jack white|neighbors blues.fact: Neighbors Blues is the closing track on Jack White's seventh solo album, Frozen Charlotte (2026, Third Man Records). It leans into the fuzzed-out garage-rock sound of his earlier records.

camp cope|the opener.fact: The Opener is the first track on Camp Cope's second album, How to Socialise & Make Friends, released March 2, 2018. The Melbourne trio's album debuted at number 6 on the Australian ARIA chart.

cheekface|i don't work here.fact: I Don't Work Here is a 2026 single from Cheekface's sixth album, Podium. It was recorded at Palmquist Studios in Los Angeles with producer Eric Palmquist, and the video was shot in a grocery store.

sufjan stevens|eugene.fact: Eugene is track 5 on Sufjan Stevens' 2015 album Carrie & Lowell, which was recorded in several places including Portland, Oregon, Norman, Oklahoma and Eau Claire, Wisconsin. Some parts were even recorded on an iPhone in a hotel room in Klamath Falls, Oregon.

overcoats|the fool.fact: The Fool was released in September 2019 on Loma Vista Recordings, marking a fresh start for the Brooklyn duo Hana Elion and JJ Mitchell, who debuted the new look with shaved heads. It was followed by an EP with two more songs, Leave If You Wanna and Keep the Faith.

jim james|come again.fact: Come Again is the lead single from Jim James' 2026 album Wowed Out on ATO Records, his first solo album in eight years. It began as a piece he composed for a scene set in a teddy bear factory, and the album grew out of music he wrote for two film projects in the early 2010s.

wilco|love is everywhere (beware).fact: Love Is Everywhere (Beware) was released as a single on July 16, 2019, ahead of Wilco's eleventh studio album, Ode to Joy, which came out October 4, 2019.

gorillaz|delirium.fact: Delirium is track 10 on The Mountain, Gorillaz's ninth studio album (February 27, 2026). It features Mark E. Smith of the post-punk band The Fall, built from outtakes of his 2010 Plastic Beach sessions.

the damned|smash it up, part i.fact: Smash It Up came out in 1979 from The Damned's third album, Machine Gun Etiquette. The band had been the first UK punk group to release a single, New Rose, back in 1976.

jens lekman|a postcard to nina.fact: A Postcard to Nina is from Jens Lekman's second album, Night Falls Over Kortedala (2007). In 2022 the album was pulled from streaming over sample clearances and reissued as The Linden Trees Are Still in Blossom.

m83|kim & jessie.fact: Kim & Jessie was the third single from M83's 2008 album Saturdays = Youth, written by Anthony and Yann Gonzalez with Morgan Kibby. Pitchfork ranked it number 5 on its best songs of 2008 and number 256 on its Top 500 Tracks of the 2000s.

kate bush|hello earth.fact: Kate Bush recorded Hounds of Love (1985) in a 48-track studio she built in a barn behind her home near London. The choir on Hello Earth is the Richard Hickox Singers performing Tsintskaro, a Georgian folk song she first heard in Werner Herzog's film Nosferatu the Vampyre.

the war on drugs|whoâ€™s that.fact: Who's That is The War on Drugs' first new single in five years. Adam Granduciel wrote and produced it at his Burbank studio, layering six- and 12-string guitars, Mellotron and vintage synths, with Alex Fischel of Spoon among the contributors.

iron & wine|woman king.fact: Woman King was the title track of an Iron & Wine EP released February 22, 2005 on Sub Pop. Sam Beam recorded it in August 2004 with Brian Deck at Engine Studios, adding percussion, piano, violin and electric guitar to his usually hushed sound.

son little|in orbit.fact: In Orbit was Son Little's first new music in three years when it arrived in 2025, and it later appeared as track 9 on his 2026 album Cityfolk. Critics described it as a blend of R&B and folk-pop.

arlo parks|2sided.fact: 2SIDED is a single from Arlo Parks' third album, Ambiguous Desire (2026, Transgressive), and swaps live instruments for synths and drum machines. The album was produced by Baird, who has worked with Brockhampton, and drew on influences like The Streets, Burial and LCD Soundsystem.

dirty projectors|stillness is the move.fact: Stillness Is the Move was the lead single from Dirty Projectors' 2009 album Bitte Orca, their first on Domino Records. Pitchfork named it the second-best track of 2009, and Solange Knowles later covered it and invited bandleader Dave Longstreth to play on her album A Seat at the Table.

iceage|ember.fact: Ember opens Iceage's sixth album, For Love of Grace & the Hereafter (May 29, 2026), their first album of new material in five years. The Danish band recorded it at Silence Studio in rural Sweden with a raw, live approach and minimal overdubs.

talking heads|this must be the place (na.fact: To keep this song simple, Talking Heads swapped instruments: bassist Tina Weymouth played guitar and guitarist Jerry Harrison played the repeating bass part on a Prophet-5 synthesizer. It closes 1983's Speaking in Tongues, and David Byrne said he wanted to write a love song that wasn't corny.

talking heads|pulled up.fact: Pulled Up is one of the closing tracks on Talking Heads' debut album, Talking Heads: 77 (September 16, 1977), and was released as a single in the UK in March 1978. The album's Super Deluxe Edition unearthed a previously unheard alternate Pop version of the song.

frankie cosmos|one of each.fact: One of Each is from Different Talking, the sixth studio album by Frankie Cosmos, released June 27, 2025 on Sub Pop in LP, CD, cassette and digital formats.

spencer krug|i'll believe in anything (2.fact: This solo piano take began at Spencer Krug's January 2026 set at Unreal City Fest in Vancouver, then was recorded at Risque Disque Records in Ladysmith, BC for release on Sub Pop. The original I'll Believe in Anything is from Wolf Parade's debut album, Apologies to the Queen Mary.

camera obscura|french navy.fact: French Navy was the first single from Camera Obscura's fourth album, My Maudlin Career, released April 13, 2009. The Glasgow band is led by singer Tracyanne Campbell.

pond|terrestrials.fact: Terrestrials is the title track of Pond's eleventh album, released June 19, 2026 on the band's own Mangovision label. When recording began they set rules of no fuzz and no ballads, aiming for an 80s Australian post-punk and new wave sound.

stereolab|transmuted matter.fact: Transmuted Matter is from Instant Holograms on Metal Film, released May 23, 2025 on Duophonic UHF Disks and Warp Records. It was Stereolab's first new album in 15 years.

blood orange|somewhere in between.fact: Somewhere in Between was released July 17, 2025 as a double single with Mind Loaded, ahead of Blood Orange's fifth album, Essex Honey (August 29, 2025). Dev Hynes' album features collaborators including Lorde, Caroline Polachek, Daniel Caesar and Mustafa.

courting|flex.fact: Flex was released July 7, 2023 as the first single from Courting's second album, New Last Name, which came out January 26, 2024. The band is from Liverpool, England.

crumb|amama.fact: Amama is the title track of Crumb's third album (May 17, 2024), produced by Johnscott Sanford and Jonathan Rado. The band is Lila Ramani, Bri Aronow, Jesse Brotter and Jonathan Gilad.

cindy lee|if you hear me crying.fact: If You Hear Me Crying is track 25 on Cindy Lee's Diamond Jubilee (2024), a 32-song album of more than two hours that was shortlisted for the Polaris Music Prize. Its animated video was directed by Phil Osborne, with cel animation by Patrick Flegel, the artist behind Cindy Lee.

ratboys|what's right?.fact: What's Right? is a single from Ratboys' album Singin' to an Empty Chair (February 6, 2026, New West Records). Julia Steiner said they treated the song like a studio experiment, stitching together three drum performances recorded in three different-sounding rooms.

mitski|working for the knife.fact: Working for the Knife was released October 5, 2021 on Dead Oceans as the lead single from Mitski's sixth album, Laurel Hell (February 4, 2022). It was her first major release since a hiatus that followed 2018's Be the Cowboy, and in the video she ceremonially discards a cowboy hat.

the tubs|stoop to me.fact: Stoop to Me is a single from Hard Life, the new album from London band The Tubs on Merge Records. Fiddle player Chris Haigh adds jangly licks, and the band calls it their most power-pop song, with nods to Bob Mould.

mac demarco|baby's wearing blue jeans.fact: Baby's Wearing Blue Jeans is from Mac DeMarco's 2012 debut album, Rock and Roll Night Club.

mac demarco|20200817 proud true toyota.fact: Proud True Toyota is part of One Wayne G, a huge 2023 collection of Mac DeMarco's home recordings, and he has played it live at Webster Hall in New York. That same year he released Five Easy Hot Dogs, an instrumental album recorded on a road trip from Los Angeles to New York, with each song named for the place it was recorded.

the lemon twigs|look for your mind.fact: Look for Your Mind! is the sixth album by The Lemon Twigs (May 8, 2026), produced by brothers Brian and Michael D'Addario. They recorded it mainly at their Brooklyn studio to 16-track tape, and bassist Eva Chambers of Tchotchke also designed the cover art.

turnover|nightjar.fact: Nightjar was released May 7, 2026 as a single with I See You and Realize, ahead of Turnover's album Down on Earth. After more than a decade on Run for Cover Records, the Virginia band released the album independently, with longtime front-of-house engineer Zac Montez producing to capture their live sound.

frankie rose|can't be wrong.fact: Can't Be Wrong is a single from Frankie Rose's sixth solo album, Hila (September 18, 2026, Born Losers / Night School). It has 80s new wave and funk-inspired rhythms, and the record features drummer Justin Welch of Elastica and saxophonist Jeff Tobias.

grandaddy|a.m. 180.fact: A.M. 180 is from Grandaddy's 1997 debut album, Under the Western Freeway, and was released as a single in 1998 with a cover of Pavement's Here on the B-side. It peaked at number 88 on the UK singles chart and is used as the theme music for the BBC Four series Charlie Brooker's Screenwipe.

field guide|rootin' for ya.fact: Rootin' For Ya, released May 24, 2024, is the project of Dylan MacDonald, who built the album from the ground up with drum machines and 1980s Yamaha synthesizers. The 10-track record has been called Field Guide's most accessible work.

fleet foxes, cole pulice, & lynn avery|t.fact: TM teams Fleet Foxes with saxophonist Cole Pulice and Lynn Avery. It was released November 22, 2024 by the Red Hot Organization as track 33 on a large charity compilation.

protomartyr|sounds we cannot hear.fact: Sounds We Cannot Hear is the first single from Hotel Usona, the seventh album from Detroit post-punk band Protomartyr (September 25, 2026, Domino). They recorded it with producer Dave Fridmann at his Tarbox Road Studios in western New York, adding horns, tubular bells and xylophone.

wild nothing|headlights on (feat. hatchi.fact: Headlights On is the first single from Hold (October 27, 2023, Captured Tracks), Wild Nothing's first album in five years. Jack Tatum's first self-produced record since his debut has Hatchie on backing vocals.

the strokes|lonely in the future.fact: Lonely in the Future is track 3 on Reality Awaits, The Strokes' first album in six years and the follow-up to 2020's The New Abnormal. The band played the song in full live for the first time in Tokyo.

dehd|light on.fact: Light On is the second single from Poetry, the fifth album from Chicago trio Dehd (May 10, 2024, Fat Possum). Ziyad Asrar of Whitney co-produced it with Jason Balla, recording at Palisade Studios in Chicago.

toro y moi|say that.fact: Say That was released January 1, 2013 as a single from Toro y Moi's album Anything in Return, and its video came out the next day, directed by HARRYS.

kiwi jr.|pure michigan.fact: Pure Michigan is a single from Blowin' Up, the fourth album from Canadian band Kiwi Jr. (August 14, 2026). Singer Jeremy Gaudet said he'd been trying to write a song about the Detroit-Windsor border for a couple of years, and it got finished once the band booked studio dates in Detroit.

the beths|straight line was a lie.fact: Straight Line Was a Lie is the title track of The Beths' fourth album, released August 29, 2025 on Anti-. Reviewers called it a headphones album for its layers of instrumentation, and frontwoman Elizabeth Stokes said linear progression is an illusion.

the new pornographers|pure sticker shock.fact: Pure Sticker Shock was the third single from The New Pornographers' album The Former Site Of (March 27, 2026, Merge Records), after Votive and Ballad of the Last Payphone. A.C. Newman said the song asks what has worth and who decides.

unknown mortal orchestra|swim and sleep.fact: Swim and Sleep (Like a Shark) was released as a single in September 2012 ahead of Unknown Mortal Orchestra's album II (February 2013). An acoustic version of the song later appeared on the companion Blue Record EP.

mgmt|time to pretend.fact: MGMT first recorded Time to Pretend on a college laptop with cheap Radio Shack microphones. Producer Dave Fridmann re-recorded it for 2007's Oracular Spectacular at Tarbox Road Studios, speeding it up slightly and adding live drums while keeping much of the original recording.

modest mouse|third side of the moon.fact: Third Side of the Moon had been a staple of Modest Mouse's live shows for two years before its release as a single from An Eraser and a Maze (June 5, 2026, Glacial Pace / Virgin Music Group). It followed the singles Look How Far and Picking Dragons Pockets.

future islands|for sure.fact: For Sure was Future Islands' first new music since 2017's The Far Field, and the lead single from their 2020 album As Long as You Are. It features Jenn Wasner of Wye Oak, and it was the first release with longtime touring drummer Mike Lowry as an official fourth member.

hot chip|devotion.fact: Devotion is a new song Hot Chip released with their greatest-hits compilation Joy in Repetition. Alexis Taylor called it a celebration of the devotion to doing the project together, and compared bandmate Joe Goddard to Brian Wilson for his dedication to making great pop.

big thief|vampire empire.fact: Vampire Empire was released as a single on September 13, 2023, backed with Born for Loving You. It was recorded and produced by Dom Monks at Teatre de Cal Eril studio in Guissona, Spain, during a tour, and became a live favorite after a performance on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert.

le tigre|phanta.fact: Phanta is from Le Tigre's 1999 self-titled debut album. The trio reunited in 2022 to play their first show in over a decade, and the song has found new fans through fan-made TikTok videos.

ekko astral|devorah.fact: Devorah is a six-minute song from Ekko Astral's debut album, pink balloons (April 17, 2024, Topshelf Records). The Washington, D.C. post-punk band's video for it was made by Kate the Cursed.

buzzcocks|boredom.fact: Boredom is on the Buzzcocks' Spiral Scratch EP, recorded December 28, 1976 at Indigo Sound Studios in Manchester with producer Martin Hannett and released in January 1977 on the band's own New Hormones label. According to the back cover, Boredom was recorded on the first take. Singer Howard Devoto left soon after to form Magazine.

hovvdy|you will go far.fact: You Will Go Far is track 9 on Big World, Hovvdy's sixth album (August 14, 2026). The band worked from instrumentals rather than finished demos with producer Ben Littlejohn, in sessions in Nashville and Asheville in fall 2025.

st. vincent|rattlesnake.fact: Rattlesnake opens St. Vincent's self-titled 2014 album, and its big fuzzed-out solo was played on Annie Clark's signature Ernie Ball Music Man guitar.

joy division|love will tear us apart.fact: Joy Division first recorded this song at Pennine Studios in Oldham on January 8, 1980, but the band and producer Martin Hannett weren't happy with it, so they redid it in March at Strawberry Studios in Stockport. The June 1980 single has since been covered in at least 168 recorded versions.

folly group|strange neighbour.fact: Strange Neighbour was released August 7, 2023 as London band Folly Group's first new music in over a year, described as a motorik slice of paranoid funk. It later became track 5 on their debut album, Down There! (January 12, 2024).

radiohead|daydreaming.fact: Daydreaming, the second single from Radiohead's A Moon Shaped Pool (2016), has a video directed by filmmaker Paul Thomas Anderson, who has used Jonny Greenwood's music in several of his films. Anderson and the band sent 35mm prints of the video to select theaters to screen.

the dead milkmen|punk rock girl.fact: Punk Rock Girl was the first single from The Dead Milkmen's 1988 album Beelzebubba, recorded at Arlyn Studios in Austin, Texas. Its video, directed by Adam Bernstein and filmed partly at Eastern State Penitentiary, got heavy play on MTV and made it the Philadelphia band's best-known song.

idles|rabbit run.fact: Rabbit Run was released July 30, 2025 for the soundtrack of Darren Aronofsky's film Caught Stealing. It continues the heavy sound of IDLES' album TANGK, and the band said they were also recording new material with Kenny Beats and Nigel Godrich.

fleet foxes|a long way past the past.fact: A Long Way Past the Past is track 6 on Fleet Foxes' 2020 album Shore, which Robin Pecknold produced. It was recorded between September 2018 and September 2020 in Hudson NY, Paris, Los Angeles and New York City with engineer Beatriz Artola, and the album was released on the autumnal equinox.

chinese american bear|take me to beijing.fact: Take Me to Beijing is on Wah!!!, the second album from Seattle duo Chinese American Bear (October 18, 2024, Moshi Moshi). Married musicians Anne Tong and Bryce Barsten write songs that move between English and Mandarin.

chinese american bear|forever lover.fact: Forever Lover (æ°¸è¿œçš„çˆ±äºº) is a 2025 single from Seattle duo Chinese American Bear, Anne Tong and Bryce Barsten, who write songs that flit between English and Mandarin.

new order|love vigilantes.fact: Love Vigilantes opens New Order's 1985 album Low-Life and was recorded in 1984 at Jam and Britannia Row studios in London. It leans on melodica and shows the influence of American country and folk music, a shift as the band moved from post-punk toward dance-rock.

ducks ltd.|train full of gasoline.fact: Train Full of Gasoline is track 4 on Harm's Way, the 2024 album from Ducks Ltd. on Carpark Records. Backing vocals come from Julia Steiner of Ratboys and Margaret McCarthy of Moontype, and Ratboys' Marcus Nuccio plays drums.

aphex twin|xtal.fact: Xtal opens Aphex Twin's debut album, Selected Ambient Works 85-92 (November 1992, Apollo Records). Richard D. James recorded the tracks on cassette, some reportedly dating back to 1985 when he was 14.

caroline rose|yip yip yow.fact: Caroline Rose wrote Yip Yip Yow about ten years ago and played it live for years before releasing a studio version on May 12, 2026, on a label Rose launched for the occasion. John Congleton produced it, Carla Azar played the live drums, and Zac Rae of Death Cab for Cutie played bass.

font|hey kekule.fact: Hey KekulÃ© was the first single from Strange Burden, the debut album from Austin five-piece Font (Acrophase Records). It draws on early-90s Manchester rave music and was inspired by a Cormac McCarthy essay about a German chemist of the same name.

the fixx|red skies.fact: Red Skies was the fourth and final single from The Fixx's debut album, Shuttered Room (MCA Records, 1982). It came out in the UK in June 1982 and in the US in January 1983, helped along by an MTV video, and reached number 13 on Billboard's Album Rock Tracks chart.

yard act|new beginnings.fact: New Beginnings is the second single from Yard Act's third album, You're Gonna Need a Little Music (July 17, 2026, Republic Records). The Leeds band recorded it in LA and Leeds with Nine Inch Nails bassist Justin Meldal-Johnsen, and it's the first time they made a record live in the same room.

courtney barnett|mantis.fact: Mantis is on Courtney Barnett's fourth album, Creature of Habit (March 27, 2026, Mom+Pop Music). She wrote it after spotting a little green praying mantis on top of her kitchen doorframe while making coffee.

hotline tnt|was i wrong?.fact: Was I Wrong? opens Hotline TNT's album Raspberry Moon (2025). Bandleader Will Anderson had mapped out the song's structure in a demo, but bassist Haylen suggested adding extra flavor during the studio sessions.

lord huron|not dead yet.fact: Not Dead Yet, released February 19, 2021, was Lord Huron's first new music since 2018's Vide Noir, and later appeared on their album Long Lost (May 21, 2021). The video shows the band performing with ghosts of musicians past on an old television set.

forth wanderers|7 months.fact: 7 Months is from The Longer This Goes On (July 18, 2025, Sub Pop), Forth Wanderers' first album in seven years. Guitarist Ben Guterl and vocalist Ava Trilling reunited in a Brooklyn coffee shop in summer 2021, and the band's Noah Yu Schifrin directed the video with his sister Elisabeth.

rilo kiley|the execution of all things.fact: The Execution of All Things is the title track of Rilo Kiley's second album (2002). The Los Angeles band, led by Jenny Lewis and Blake Sennett, went to Nebraska to record it with Bright Eyes' Mike Mogis and new drummer Jason Boesel.

wednesday|wound up here (by holdin on).fact: Karly Hartzman borrowed the chorus line from a poem in her friend Evan Gray's book Thickets Swamped in Fence-Coated Briars and wrote the rest of the song around it. It's from Wednesday's sixth album, Bleeds (September 19, 2025, Dead Oceans), produced by Alex Farrar, and the first to feature bassist Ethan Baechtold.

telehealth|donor country (a good cause).fact: Donor Country (A gOoD cAuSe) is from Green World Image, Telehealth's debut album on Sub Pop (May 15, 2026). Its video imagines a talent show with witches, hedge trimmers, magicians and bubblegum blowers.

coral grief|air between us.fact: Air Between Us is the title track of Coral Grief's debut album (July 18, 2025, Suicide Squeeze). The Seattle trio recorded it at The Unknown in Anacortes, Washington, a former church turned sail factory turned studio, and cites Stereolab and Broadcast as influences.

ron gallo|do you love your company.fact: Do You Love Your Company? is track 5 on Ron Gallo's Stardust Birthday Party (October 5, 2018, New West Records). In the video, Gallo confronts many versions of himself.

tv on the radio|crying.fact: Crying is from TV on the Radio's 2008 album Dear Science, which the band followed in 2011 with Nine Types of Light on Interscope Records.

ween|the argus.fact: The Argus is from Quebec, Ween's eighth studio album, released August 5, 2003. The roughly five-minute song builds to a guitar solo from Dean Ween (Mickey Melchiondo) and takes its imagery from the many-eyed giant Argus of Greek mythology.

wilco|i'm a wheel.fact: I'm a Wheel comes from Wilco's fifth studio album, A Ghost Is Born (June 22, 2004), and was released as a single on July 26, 2004.

altin gun|neredesin sen.fact: Neredesin Sen opens Garip, the sixth album from Dutch band AltÄ±n GÃ¼n (February 20, 2026, ATO Records), a tribute to Anatolian folk giant NeÅŸet ErtaÅŸ. It reworks a Turkish folk standard with a throbbing bass line and an early-80s indie feel.

grandaddy|way we won't.fact: Way We Won't was released as a single on September 9, 2016, ahead of Grandaddy's fifth album, Last Place (March 3, 2017), their first in about 14 years after 2003's Sumday.

polia|dreams go.fact: Dreams Go is the title track of PoliÃ§a's sixth album (October 17, 2025), eight songs recorded at Pachyderm Studio in Minnesota. It was produced by Ryan Olson with guest production from Peder Mannerfelt.

alvvays|adult diversion.fact: Adult Diversion was released October 28, 2013 as the second single from Alvvays' self-titled debut album, where it's the first track (July 22, 2014). Molly Rankin, Alec O'Hanley and Brian Murphy wrote it.

pavement|grounded.fact: Grounded is on Pavement's 1995 album Wowee Zowee, recorded in November 1994 at Easley Recording in Memphis, Tennessee, with more sessions in New York the following February. The song dates back to the Crooked Rain, Crooked Rain era.

geese|taxes.fact: Taxes was the lead single from Geese's fourth album, Getting Killed, released July 8, 2025 ahead of the album (September 26, 2025). The band recorded the album in Los Angeles over a month with producer Kenny Beats.

the clash|this is england.fact: This Is England was released September 30, 1985 as the lead and only single from the Clash's sixth and final album. The song leans on a drum machine and synthesizers, and Joe Strummer called it his last great Clash song.

kurt vile|chance to bleed.fact: Chance to Bleed is a single from Kurt Vile's tenth studio album, Philadelphia's Been Good to Me (May 29, 2026, Verve Forecast). Vile started the album in late 2023 and recorded much of it in his basement studio, with guest vocals on the song from Natalie Hoffman, Ethan Buckler and Greg Cartwright.

tame impala|music to walk home by.fact: Music to Walk Home By is on Tame Impala's 2012 album Lonerism. Kevin Parker wrote and produced the song himself, and it runs 5 minutes 12 seconds.

futurebirds|easy company (feat. waxahatc.fact: Easy Company is the title track of Futurebirds' fifth album (August 9, 2024, Dualtone), on which Waxahatchee's Katie Crutchfield trades verses with Carter King. The Athens, Georgia band recorded it with producer Brad Cook in the border town of Tornillo, Texas.

vampire weekend|young lion.fact: Young Lion closes Vampire Weekend's 2013 album Modern Vampires of the City. It's the only Vampire Weekend song where Rostam Batmanglij is the sole lead vocalist and writer.

lcd soundsystem|daft punk is playing at.fact: Daft Punk Is Playing at My House was recorded in 2003-04 at Long View Farm in Massachusetts and Plantain Recording House in New York, produced by DFA. It became LCD Soundsystem's biggest single, earning a Grammy nomination for Best Dance Recording and reaching number 29 on the UK chart.

westside cowboy|pin up boys.fact: Pin Up Boys is a single from It Goes On, the debut album from Manchester four-piece Westside Cowboy (August 21, Island Records). The band wrote it using an acoustic guitar, a drum machine sample pad and screwdrivers as drumsticks, then recorded it at Greenmount Studios in Leeds with producer Loren Humphrey.

wilder.|hang up.fact: Hang Up is from the debut EP Bad Bad Luck (August 2021) by Wilder., a Long Beach, California duo of guitarist and vocalist Stephen Ramos and drummer Nick Sturz.

way dynamic|officially.fact: Officially was released August 5, 2026 as a new song on the Jagjaguwar reissue of Massive Shoe, the album from Melbourne musician Dylan Young, who records as Way Dynamic.

horse jumper of love|heartbreak rules.fact: Heartbreak Rules is the title track of a mini-album released May 19, 2023: eight new songs, two reworked tracks from Natural Part and a cover of The Smashing Pumpkins' Luna. Dimitri Giannopoulos wrote and recorded it alone, stripping away the band's usual fuzz for a sparse sound.

the sophs|sweat.fact: SWEAT is from GOLDSTAR (March 13, 2026), the album from The Sophs, who signed to Rough Trade after their demos impressed label founders Geoff Travis and Jeannette Lee.

panda bear, sonic boom & adrian sherwood.fact: This is dub legend Adrian Sherwood's remix of Whirlpool, from Reset in Dub (August 18, 2023), a reimagining of Panda Bear and Sonic Boom's 2022 album Reset. Sherwood built it at his On-U Sound Studios with musicians including Doug Wimbish and Skip McDonald, who played with Sugarhill Gang and Grandmaster Flash.

the durutti column|liars.fact: Liars is a single from Renascent (July 31, 2026), the first Durutti Column album of new material since 2010. Guitarist Vini Reilly made it with longtime collaborator Keir Stewart, pairing his distinctive guitar sound with chilled club beats.

panda bear & sonic boom|graveyard.fact: Graveyard is one side of a 7-inch single with Lucky Charm, two new Panda Bear and Sonic Boom songs released April 18, 2026 on Domino as a Record Store Day exclusive.

mj lenderman|just be simple.fact: Just Be Simple is MJ Lenderman's cover of a Songs: Ohia song, recorded for the tribute album I Will Swim to You: A Tribute to Jason Molina. It was released as a preview in September 2025 and pressed on a limited 7-inch on January 23, 2026.
